description: Creates a 1500-line comprehensive analysis collating information from all documents in a project, focusing on overall details rather than migration-specific recommendations
text:
You are a senior technical analyst tasked with creating comprehensive project-level insights by collating information from all processed documents.

Project Name: {{project_name}}
Total Documents Analyzed: {{document_count}}

Document Assessments:
{{all_assessments}}

Extracted Facts Across All Documents:
{{all_facts}}

Generate a comprehensive analysis of this project in EXACTLY 1500 lines or less. Your analysis should collate and synthesize information from all documents to provide a complete picture of the project.

Structure your insights with the following sections:

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (100-150 lines)
- Overall project scope and purpose
- Key systems and components identified
- Primary technologies and platforms in use
- Critical findings across all documents
- Project completeness assessment
- High-level observations and patterns

## 2. COMPREHENSIVE TECHNOLOGY LANDSCAPE (200-250 lines)
### 2.1 Programming Languages & Frameworks
- All programming languages identified across documents
- Frameworks and libraries in use
- Version information where available
- Technology stack patterns

### 2.2 Platforms & Operating Systems
- Operating systems (Unix, Linux, Windows, etc.)
- Cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.)
- Containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes, etc.)
- Platform versions and configurations

### 2.3 Tools & Utilities
- Development tools
- Build and deployment tools
- Monitoring and logging tools
- Integration tools

## 3. INFRASTRUCTURE & ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW (200-250 lines)
### 3.1 System Inventory
- Complete list of systems identified
- Server types and roles
- Hardware specifications where documented
- System interdependencies

### 3.2 Network Architecture
- Network topology patterns
- Connectivity between systems
- Load balancing and redundancy
- Network security boundaries

### 3.3 Deployment Architecture
- Deployment models (cloud, on-premise, hybrid)
- High availability configurations
- Disaster recovery setups
- Scalability patterns

## 4. DATA ECOSYSTEM (150-200 lines)
### 4.1 Data Stores & Databases
- All databases identified (SQL, NoSQL, etc.)
- Database versions and configurations
- Data distribution patterns
- Replication and backup strategies

### 4.2 Data Management
- Data models and schemas
- Data flow patterns across systems
- ETL/ELT processes
- Data retention and archival policies

### 4.3 Data Quality & Governance
- Data quality measures
- Data governance frameworks
- Master data management
- Data lineage tracking

## 5. SECURITY POSTURE (150-200 lines)
### 5.1 Authentication & Authorization
- Authentication mechanisms in use
- Authorization models
- Identity management systems
- Single sign-on implementations

### 5.2 Data Protection
- Encryption methods (at rest, in transit)
- Key management practices
- Data masking and tokenization
- Privacy controls

### 5.3 Security Controls
- Firewall configurations
- Intrusion detection/prevention
- Security monitoring
- Vulnerability management

### 5.4 Compliance & Standards
- Compliance requirements (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2, etc.)
- Security standards followed
- Audit trails and logging
- Regulatory considerations

## 6. OPERATIONAL INSIGHTS (150-200 lines)
### 6.1 Monitoring & Observability
- Monitoring solutions in place
- Metrics and KPIs tracked
- Alerting mechanisms
- Dashboarding and visualization

### 6.2 Performance & Scalability
- Performance characteristics
- Scalability patterns
- Resource utilization
- Performance optimization strategies

### 6.3 Maintenance & Support
- Backup and recovery processes
- Patching and update procedures
- Support models
- Incident management

## 7. INTEGRATION & CONNECTIVITY (100-150 lines)
- Integration patterns used
- APIs and services exposed
- External system dependencies
- Data exchange formats
- Message queuing and event streaming

## 8. DOCUMENTATION QUALITY ASSESSMENT (75-100 lines)
- Completeness of documentation across project
- Consistency in documentation quality
- Areas with strong documentation
- Gaps in documentation coverage
- Technical accuracy observations
- Documentation standards adherence

## 9. CROSS-CUTTING CONCERNS (100-150 lines)
- Logging and auditing practices
- Configuration management
- Secrets management
- Environment management (dev, test, prod)
- Disaster recovery readiness
- Business continuity planning

## 10. KEY FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS (100-150 lines)
- Critical patterns identified across documents
- Technology standardization vs. diversity
- Architectural consistency
- Common themes and recurring elements
- Notable configurations or setups
- Unique or unusual implementations
- Areas of technical debt
- Innovation and modern practices

## 11. KNOWLEDGE GAPS & RECOMMENDATIONS (75-100 lines)
- Information missing from documentation
- Areas requiring additional documentation
- Questions that remain unanswered
- Suggestions for documentation improvement
- Areas needing further investigation
- Recommended next steps for complete understanding

IMPORTANT FORMATTING RULES:
1. Use markdown headers (##, ###, ####) for hierarchical structure
2. Use bullet points (-) and numbered lists as appropriate
3. Keep each point concise yet informative (1-3 lines)
4. STRICTLY adhere to the 1500-line total limit
5. If a section is not applicable, state "Not applicable - no relevant information found" rather than omitting
6. Use **bold** for critical information and key terms
7. Be specific with names, versions, counts, and technical details
8. Cross-reference related information across sections when relevant
9. Prioritize factual synthesis over speculation
10. Provide actual examples and specifics from the documents
11. Use tables (markdown format) where appropriate for comparing information
12. Include quantitative data where available (counts, versions, sizes, etc.)

Generate the comprehensive project insights now, collating all information from the provided assessments and facts:
